title: Graph evaluation and transition inverses for the etale tuple module
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $(q_i:V_i\to F)_{i\in I}$ a set-indexed family of etale maps from schemes, not necessarily jointly surjective. Work in a universe containing $I$, all section sets and the products below, and a small skeleton of $F_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $R_{ij}=V_i\times_F V_j$, with projections $p_i,p_j$; all displayed fibre products are schemes by the representable diagonal. Let $L_i$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O_{(V_i)_{\mathrm{et}}}$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Restrictions to overlaps are restrictions on localized etale sites. Suppose now that $a_{ij}:L_j|_{(R_{ij})_{\mathrm{et}}}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_i|_{(R_{ij})_{\mathrm{et}}}$ are module isomorphisms, their pullbacks along $V_i\to R_{ii}$ are identities, and $a_{ik}=a_{ij}a_{jk}$ on every $V_i\times_FV_j\times_FV_k$, using the canonical composition identifications. Let $M$ be the module sheaf whose sections, restrictions and module operations are the explicit compatible-tuple formulas of [lem-trf-space-etale-module-tuple-sheaf]; thus $M(W)$ consists of tuples $s_i\in L_i(W\times_FV_i)$ satisfying $s_i|_{W_{ij}}=a_{ij}(s_j|_{W_{ij}})$. For each $a\in I$ and each etale $t:W\to V_a$, put $W_i=W\times_FV_i$ and let $d_a=(1_W,t):W\to W_a$. Define
$$e_{a,W}:M(W\to F)\longrightarrow L_a(W),\qquad (s_i)\longmapsto d_a^*s_a,$$
and
$$j_{a,W}:L_a(W)\longrightarrow M(W\to F),\qquad y\longmapsto\bigl(a_{ia}(y|_{W_i})\bigr)_i.$$
In the latter formula $a_{ia}$ is evaluated using $W_i\to R_{ia}$ with components $W_i\to V_i$ and $W_i\to W\xrightarrow t V_a$, and $y|_{W_i}$ is restriction on $(V_a)_{\mathrm{et}}$. These formulas are well-defined linear maps, natural in every morphism $W'\to W$ over $V_a$, and satisfy $e_{a,W}j_{a,W}=1$ and $j_{a,W}e_{a,W}=1$. Consequently they give module-sheaf isomorphisms $e_a:q_a^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}L_a$ whose inverses have exactly the displayed formula. For every $a,b$ and every etale test scheme $W\to R_{ab}$, the resulting maps satisfy $e_{a,W}=a_{ab,W}e_{b,W}$. This includes $a=b$ with two different lifts of $W$ to $V_a$; identity for $a_{aa}$ is assumed only on the diagonal. No local freeness or joint-surjectivity hypothesis is required.

proof.text: All products used below are schemes: each $W\times_FV_i$ is a scheme by representability of $q_i$, and iterate this observation for triple products. Base change and composition in [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] make their structural maps to $F$ etale. Its cancellation clause makes every map between these scheme objects over $F$ etale. In particular $W_i\to W$, the graphs $d_a$, and the graph maps to triple products used below are legitimate arrows on the localized sites. A morphism $W\to V_a$ over $F$ is etale by the same cancellation clause. Thus postcomposition identifies $(V_a)_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $F_{\mathrm{et}}/V_a$: the inverse forgets the composite to $F$, and both functors leave the underlying scheme arrows and covering families unchanged. The structure rings agree since both evaluate on a scheme $T$ as $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ [def-trf-algebraic-space].

Use the exact section and restriction formulas of [lem-trf-space-etale-module-tuple-sheaf]. For $y\in L_a(W)$ set $z_i=a_{ia}(y|_{W_i})$. On $W_{ij}$ the cocycle pulled back along $(W_{ij}\to V_i,W_{ij}\to V_j,W_{ij}\to W\xrightarrow t V_a)$ gives
$$a_{ij}(z_j|_{W_{ij}})=a_{ij}a_{ja}(y|_{W_{ij}})=a_{ia}(y|_{W_{ij}})=z_i|_{W_{ij}}.$$
Naturality of each transition morphism justifies restricting $z_i$ in this equality. Hence $z$ lies in $M(W)$ and defines $j_{a,W}$. The other map $e_{a,W}$ is defined by restricting the $a$ coordinate along the arrow $d_a$ from step 1.

proof.text:
The two maps are $\mathcal O_F(W)=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$-linear. For $b\in\mathcal O_F(W)$, the tuple-module scalar formula gives
$$e_{a,W}(bs)=d_a^*((b|_{W_a})s_a)=b\,d_a^*s_a,$$
since $\operatorname{pr}_W d_a=1_W$; and $a_{ia}((b|_{W_i})(y|_{W_i}))=(b|_{W_i})a_{ia}(y|_{W_i})$ by the assumed module-linearity. Addition and zero follow by the same coordinatewise formulas. For $f:W'\to W$ over $V_a$, let $f_i:W'_i\to W_i$ preserve both projections. The equality $f_a d'_a=d_af$ follows by comparing the two projections. Therefore $e_{a,W'}(s|_{W'})=e_{a,W}(s)|_{W'}$. Naturality of $a_{ia}$ gives $(j_{a,W}(y))_i|_{W'_i}=a_{ia}(y|_{W'_i})=(j_{a,W'}(y|_{W'}))_i$, proving naturality of $j$.

source.place: Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves), proof: explicit compatible tuples and omitted local isomorphisms/commutative diagrams; graph calculations supplied by Q24.

proof.text: In $e_{a,W}j_{a,W}(y)=d_a^*a_{aa}(y|_{W_a})$, the map $W_a\to R_{aa}$ used in $a_{aa}$ has components $(\operatorname{pr}_{V_a},t\operatorname{pr}_W)$. Composing with $d_a$ gives $(t,t)=\Delta_at$. By naturality this composite is $(\Delta_a^*a_{aa})(y)=y$, using precisely the assumed diagonal normalization and $\operatorname{pr}_Wd_a=1_W$. We do not assert that $a_{aa}$ is the identity on all of $R_{aa}$.

source.place: Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves), proof: explicit compatible tuples and omitted local isomorphisms/commutative diagrams; graph calculations supplied by Q24.

proof.text:
For $s\in M(W)$ and $i\in I$, pull its $(i,a)$ compatibility equation on $W\times_FV_i\times_FV_a$ back along
$$h_i:W_i\longrightarrow W\times_FV_i\times_FV_a,\qquad (w,v_i)\longmapsto(w,v_i,t(w)).$$
These coordinate formulas mean the unique maps with the displayed projections. Its projection to $W_i$ is the identity and its projection to $W_a$ is $d_a\operatorname{pr}_W$. Naturality of $a_{ia}$ therefore gives
$$s_i=a_{ia}\bigl(\operatorname{pr}_W^*d_a^*s_a\bigr)=(j_{a,W}e_{a,W}(s))_i.$$
Equality of every coordinate is equality of tuples, so $j_{a,W}e_{a,W}=1$.

source.place: Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves), proof: explicit compatible tuples and omitted local isomorphisms/commutative diagrams; graph calculations supplied by Q24.

proof.text:
By step 1 and the restriction convention of [def-trf-algebraic-space], $q_a^*M(W\to V_a)=M(W\to F)$. The natural linear maps in step 3 are module-sheaf morphisms by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and steps 4 and 5 give their two inverse identities, hence the asserted isomorphism with the specified inverse. For $W\to R_{ab}$ write its two lifts as $t_a,t_b$. Pull the $(a,b)$ tuple equation back along
$$h_{ab}:W\to W\times_FV_a\times_FV_b,\qquad w\mapsto(w,t_a(w),t_b(w)).$$
Its projections are $d_a$ and $d_b$. Naturality gives $d_a^*s_a=a_{ab,W}(d_b^*s_b)$, which is exactly $e_{a,W}=a_{ab,W}e_{b,W}$. This argument also applies when $a=b$ and $t_a\ne t_b$, without using diagonal normalization there. No step used joint surjectivity or local freeness.
